en: What does it mean that value in a Place has "no sign"?

options.en: That the value is zero or null if everyone contributes.
That there are no indications on how to understand value.
That its valence (positive or negative) depends on the subjective experience of the user.
That the government has decided not to give clear indications on the strategy.

explain: Place value has no fixed sign — users may perceive it as positive or negative.

en: In the "Product" lever, the "Place Value Proposition" is defined as:

options.en: A system of physical elements representing the value of the place.
A package of benefits and solutions that the place-system intends to offer to users.
The sum of all tangible elements of the place.
The intangible elements of the place.
Excessive tourism degrades resources and limits the quality of life of residents.
The place marketing plan reaches the maximum success foreseen by the budget.
Numerous opportunities that come from a correct tourist strategy.
The territory receives funding to build tourist opportunities.

en: What is a crucial challenge for "Onplace" Universities in the New Normal?

options.en: Becoming e-learning centers.
Using online activity to generate the need to physically experience the local university life.
Increasing the presence of new technological infrastructures.
Encouraging the presence of students who study online.

explain: Onplace universities use online to strengthen the desire for on-campus, local experience.

en: How can a museum offer an "onlife" experience?

options.en: By closing physical rooms and offering virtual tours.
By integrating human guides with robots that repeat customized information.
By integrating the use of smartphones inside exhibition areas.
By integrating the physical path with digital contents that enrich the meaning of the visit.

en: "Knowledge diffusion" is the responsibility of the local government because:

options.en: It is the only entity that legally possesses the rights to the historical truth of the place.
It creates the pre-conditions so that actors can connect and co-create value.
It serves to explain political choices to the population.
It multiplies the dissemination of culture.

en: A Place in Quadrant "d" has a high level of democracy but suffers from:

options.en: Difficulties in evolution and adaptation to new market challenges.
Lack of dialogue among citizens.
An excessive exploitation of resources.
An internet connection that is too fast and distracts the inhabitants.

en: The "Survival" purpose of a territorial system (VSA) depends on its:

options.en: Amount of capital useful to manage the city's activities.
Ability to maintain the balance between internal variety and external variability.
Ability to plan with the collaboration of administrators.
Defining strategic objectives.

en: Who are considered the "primary stakeholders" of a place?

options.en: International tourists who contribute to economic development.
Large multinationals looking for production sites to provide employment.
Residents and citizens who live in the territory daily.
Rating agencies that assess the financial soundness of the local entity.
The positioning of a website in global search engines.
The spatial context in which it is possible to enjoy the value proposition.
The way shops are organized in the city.
The urban organization of TCM.
The abandonment of the current vocation to attract new industrial sectors.
The optimization of existing resources by reinforcing the current territorial vocation.
The sale of natural resources to finance local public debt.
Encouraging citizens to carry on their traditions.
Individual goals are in strong conflict with the ultimate purpose of the place-system.
Two people actively participate in living labs.
Living labs do not work.
Tourists and residents have the same interests.

en: According to the Viable Systems Approach (VSA), a system is "viable" if:

options.en: It possesses a high endowment of tangible resources.
It is isolated from global market dynamics to preserve its identity.
It is capable of surviving over time by adapting to changes in the context and environment.
It possesses a high endowment of intangible resources.

en: What characterizes Quadrant "b" (Medium technology, Medium relationship)?

options.en: A smart city evolving according to value co-creation.
Absence of operational territorial marketing.
A Demand-driven approach focused on satisfying a specific target.
A technological dictatorship that limits the real needs of residents.

en: What is the main risk of the presence of "free-riders" in a CCN project?

options.en: The depletion of collective resources due to those who benefit from advantages without contributing.
An excessive increase in commercial competition among shops in the same center.
The closure of small independent shops in favor of extra-urban shopping malls.
Excessive tax pressure on residential property owners.
Because it is a constraint imposed by the regulations and directives of the European Commission.
To increase the number of physical participants at technical and political tables.
Because true innovation does not exist without the active and convinced participation of the system of actors.
To multiply the decision-making autonomy of primary stakeholders and the government.

en: The role of the University in a place strategy is that of:

options.en: Catalyst and provider of knowledge for the application of the marketing framework to marketing management.
Catalyst and provider of knowledge for attracting investments.
Catalyst and provider of knowledge for brand development.
Catalyst and provider of value through the dissemination of knowledge, projects, and human capital.

en: What is meant by "Place Brand Equity"?

options.en: The systematic result of the place's image and identity in the minds of stakeholders.
The total equity value expressed in euros of the city's brand.
The brand of the natural shopping center born from the TCM model.
The value of the total visitors to the city center.

en: The concept of "Mutuality" implies that actors:

options.en: Participate in the co-design of the marketing plan.
Help each other to overcome the economic crisis.
Work for a common ultimate purpose, sharing expectations, risks, and strategic results.
All possess the same annual income level and professional qualification.
